skill_description: When adding a project, module, or file, put it on a capability path so directory hierarchy, directory names, and file names express product capabilities (package-by-feature / vertical slices), not technical layers. Use this skill when creating a new project or service tree, adding a feature and choosing its home, deciding where a file or package goes, naming folders and files, splitting or merging modules, migrating off layered trees (controllers/services, domain/application/infrastructure, clean/hexagonal/onion), reviewing or restructuring folder layout, designing an agent-friendly or AI-readable codebase, or when the user mentions repo layout, project structure, screaming architecture, package by feature, feature-first, or vertical slice. Also use when adding code and the home must be obvious from the path alone. Not for touring a tree with no layout change, cosmetic tidy with no boundary problem, domain glossaries, module-depth or seam design, or numbered agent-workflow workspaces (01-spec/02-design).
method: Given only skill name + description (no SKILL.md body), decide load YES/NO for each user message.

cases.prompt: New service. How should we organize the project directory so folder and file names show what the product does?

Review this folder layout and migrate it to package-by-feature / vertical slices.

Agent keeps dropping files in utils/. Set a repo layout so path + filename express the capability.
Our backend is clean/hexagonal: src/domain, src/application, src/infrastructure. Reorganize so capabilities scream from the path.
shared/ is a junk drawer (auth, money, orders, http). Split ownership before adding another helper.
We're all AI-agent development now and cannot review every line. Design an agent-friendly folder tree so directory names are the architecture.
Next.js App Router — where should checkout pricing rules live? app/ is mostly routes today.
Greenfield Go module: HTTP API. How should cmd/ and internal/ relate to billing and identity?
This PR put refund logic in src/utils/refund.ts. Review placement only.

Alphabetize the folders and unify README formatting. No boundary or placement problem.
Add the term Refund to CONTEXT.md and write an ADR for picking Postgres.
